sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic heritage with common-law-inspired commercial and private foundation statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: U.S.–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012)
Double Taxation Agreements concluded 2019–2023 with the Netherlands, Mexico, Spain, Luxembourg, UAE, Qatar, Portugal and Ireland (territorial tax model)
Hague Apostille Convention (in force for Panama since 31 July 1995)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT); Executive Decree No. 1 of 15 July 2016 (AML/CFT implementing regulations); Ley No. 254 of 19 November 2021 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) as amended; Executive Decree No. 296 of 21 October 2022 (UBO registry regulations); Ley No. 25 of 12 June 1995 and Ley No. 9 of 2018 (Private Interest Foundations); Ley 38 of 31 July 2000 (administrative procedure).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Charter (Carta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized in Panama; no apostille required for a Panamanian instrument; registration with the DGRM within 30 days of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney to incorporate or register the Foundation, executed by the founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the founder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (member states) or Consular Legalization (non-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarial or consular copy of the founder's and UBO's passport or national identification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary or consulate of the Republic of Panama

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / source-of-funds due diligence letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; accepted as part of the resident agent's AML/KYC file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the founder, all foundation council members, any protector, the resident agent, and disclosed UBOs against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK OFSI list, and Panama's UAF designated persons list. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is triggered for PEPs, high-risk origin jurisdictions, or incomplete source-of-funds documentation. At least two independent electronic screening databases must be consulted; the complete screening record, adverse-hit resolutions, and KYC documentation must be retained by the resident agent and filed with the DGRM for not less than five (5) years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas y Titulares de Fideicomiso (DGRM) — Ministerio de Gobierno, Republic of Panama (official online name clearance request through the DGRM public portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be in Spanish, English, or any language using the Latin alphabet. The name must include the suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado' (or the accepted abbreviation 'FIP' / 'PIF') and must be clearly distinguishable from all registered entity names. All registry filings must be submitted in Spanish; foreign-language names must be accompanied by a Spanish transliteration for the registry index.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Trust (where implying grant of a banking trust licence)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days and is non-extendable; on expiry a new application with a new search must be filed. Upon a DGRM refusal, the applicant may within 8 business days file a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) under Article 92 of Ley 38 of 2000 before the same authority, followed, if dismissed, by a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) to the Minister of Government within 5 business days. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately reserve an alternative distinguishable name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited. The Foundation must maintain a Panama-domiciled Resident Agent (an attorney licensed as 'abogado idóneo', or registered fiduciary) at a physical address for service of process. A 'virtual office' is permissible only as a service desk operated within the Resident Agent's physical Panamanian premises; a postal-box-only address without human presence is not compliant. Operational management of the online luxury resale business may be conducted remotely; the registered seat remains the Resident Agent's official address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Medium: for a newly constituted PIF in the medium-risk e-commerce segment, the probability of an unannounced on-site or electronic inspection by the DGRM or the UAF within the first 12 months is estimated at 10–15%; the likelihood increases materially upon screening alerts, incomplete UBO disclosure, or unusual payment flows through Stripe or Escrow.Pay rails.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Foundation Charter (Carta Constitutiva) and annexes
Registration of the Foundation with the DGRM Private Interest Foundation Registry
Initial UBO filing (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — UBO Registry Office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Resident agent first-year fee (service of process, AML file custody, regulatory proxy)
Apostille / consular legalization of power of attorney and identification documents (2 documents)
Pre-incorporation AML/KYC screening (two international databases, OFAC/UN/EU/UK/UAF)
Foundation Charter drafting, corporate governance schedule, and compliance review — legal fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law 41 of 2016, Articles 1–50; Executive Decree No. 65 of 2013; Regulation of the Public Registry of Panama on Juridical Persons.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Juridical Persons Section); Municipalidad de Panamá for local commercial licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional / Acto Constitutivo) executed as a public deed (Escritura Pública) before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies under Law 25 of 1995; the founder may allocate nominal assets (from USD 100), with no legally mandated escrow account or deposit requirement. Licensed resident agents commonly recommend an initial endowment of USD 10,000 for commercial credibility, contributed as a declared non-refundable capital allocation to the foundation estate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 001 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME], a Private Interest Foundation of Panama. The undersigned Foundation Council, exercising powers under Law 25 of 1995 and the Foundation Charter, resolves: (1) the Foundation Charter is adopted and filed with the Public Registry of Panama; (2) the initial endowment of USD 10,000 is subscribed; (3) the registered office is established at [City of Panama address] and the Resident Agent is appointed; (4) [names] are appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer, each for a one-year term; and (5) counsel is authorized to execute ancillary filings. Unanimously approved on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Juridical Person Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Ventanilla Única de Personas Jurídicas; online portal www.registro-publico.gob.pa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed foundation names in Spanish or English through the online name-search module or in person. Pay the nominal search fee and obtain the Certificate of Name Availability (Certificado de Disponibilidad del Nombre), valid for 30 days, before drafting the charter.
required_dossiers: Completed online name-search application
Foundation purpose summary in Spanish
Three proposed name variants
Identification copy of founder (passport or corporate ID)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, already assigned, or reserved by a third party, file a revised application with new name variants; the registry fee is credited toward the next submission and no formal appeal is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Foundation Charter before a Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública (Notary Public of the Republic of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder or authorized representative appears before a Panamanian notary to execute the public deed containing the Foundation Charter, including: foundation name, purpose (online consignment and secondhand luxury goods retail), allocated assets, Foundation Council members, founder's reserved powers (amendment, revocation, appointment of protectors), beneficiary designation, registered office, and resident agent appointment. The notary issues the Escritura Pública and notarial testimony for registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Name Availability
Draft Foundation Charter and Bylaws (Estatutos)
Founder's identification and proof of authority if corporate founder
Identity documents of initial Foundation Council members
Resident agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary will correct drafting inconsistencies or request a new execution hearing; missing consents or incomplete council-member data are cured by supplementary sworn affidavits without registry penalties at this pre-filing stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration (Inscripción) in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Sección de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial testimony together with supporting exhibits, pay the registry folio fee and stamp taxes online or at the cashier, and obtain the adaptation stamp. The foundation is legally incorporated upon folio inscription (protocolización). Retrieve the certified registration copy (Copia Registrada) and the registered Foundation Charter with marginal annotations.
required_dossiers: Original notarial Escritura Pública
Certificate of Name Availability
Payment receipt for registry fees and stamp taxes
Resident agent license and acceptance letter
Cover letter from the sponsoring law firm or licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a calificación or formal query, respond within five business days with the corrective exhibit or an amended charter clause; the registry completes a second review within three days, and a rejected filing may be re-submitted once without new fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Commercial License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá or the Municipality of the district of the registered office, Dirección General de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation's economic activity in the municipal taxpayer roll and obtain the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) and municipal business patent (Patente Municipal). The activity is coded as retail trade via internet and consignment of secondhand luxury goods; ensure zoning compliance for office and light warehousing use of the registered address.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Lease agreement or title deed proving lawful use of the registered office
Taxpayer registration (RUC/NIT) issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos
Identification of the legal representative and Foundation Council members
Completed municipal application form for Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal queries are cured by submitting an updated zoning certificate, landlord consent, or corrected lease; if the permit is refused, an appeal may be filed with the Municipal Board of Appeals within fifteen business days, with provisional operation allowed under the receipt of application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Inscription Formalities and Foundation Council Installation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, through the licensed resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, obtain certified copies of the registered charter, open the statutory books (Foundation Council minute book and members/beneficiaries register), and convene the first Foundation Council meeting to adopt Resolution No. 001. Apply to DGI for the taxpayer registration number (RUC/NIT) and, as applicable, file the notice of territorial taxation basis; open a Panamanian bank account for the endowment and e-commerce settlement funds.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Public Registry inscription
Foundation Council resolution appointing officers
DGI RUC/NIT application forms
Anti-money laundering compliance documentation for the foundation file
Original first board resolution and officer acceptance letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Missing exhibits are re-filed directly with the registry or DGI; late municipal or tax registration penalties may be waived if the application is submitted within thirty days of the certificate date, supported by the inscription proof.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries of Panama (MICI), Directorate of Trade Regulations; Municipalidad de Panamá, Department of Economic Activities and Used Goods Control
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Aviso de Operación with Secondhand Goods Dealer Endorsement (Permiso Municipal de Compraventa y Consignación de Artículos Usados), registered with MICI and the municipal revenue office

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (MiAMBIENTE), National Directorate of Environmental Verification
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II — Simplified Environmental Registration (Declaración de Impacto Ambiental, abbreviated) or Environmental Registration Certificate. Full EIA (Category III) is not required for commercial warehousing and online retail below 5,000 m², provided no industrial processing or hazardous waste generation occurs.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Executive Decree No. 505 of 2002 and national water quality criteria for any sanitary discharges; prohibition of unpermitted process wastewater; segregated solid-waste management and disposal per Law 33 of 2007 and Executive Decree No. 179 of 2020; no ozone-depleting substances; storage of leather, textile, and accessories in sealed containers with VOC-free protocols; light-commercial HVAC maintenance records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado de Seguridad Contra Incendios) from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá; structural load verification and occupancy clearance from the municipal Directorate of Works and Constructions; occupational hygiene and sanitation clearance from the Ministry of Health (MINSA); workplace ergonomics, electrical, and risk assessments per MITRADEL Resolution No. 022-2021 for office and warehouse staff.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a central bank or a dedicated foreign-exchange administration. Banking, treasury, and FX-conduct supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Decree Law 9 of 1998, as amended. The Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) enforces AML/CFT reporting standards, while Banco Nacional de Panamá performs clearing and agency functions without exercising monetary policy or currency-issuance authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully dollarized economy: the US dollar is legal tender and the Panamanian Balboa circulates only as subsidiary coinage at a fixed 1:1 rate. Both current and capital accounts are completely open, with no registration, licensing, approval, or exchange-control restrictions on inward or outward transfers. Profit and dividend remittances face zero FX or conversion hurdles; the only fiscal friction is the territorial-tax framework, which applies a 10% withholding or final tax to Panama-source distributions on a defined basis, while foreign-source income realized by the Private Interest Foundation (PIF), including online resale proceeds settled through Stripe and Escrow_Pay, is outside the Panamanian tax net provided the business is managed and executed abroad. No Balboa/U.S.-dollar exchange-control band exists, so convertibility risk is effectively nil.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation/surrender requirement for export or e-commerce proceeds. The PIF may retain 100% of USD receivables in Panamanian or offshore accounts and is free to switch currencies at will. Compliance obligations are confined to banking record-keeping and UAF reporting thresholds: cash and individual wire transactions of USD 10,000 or more, or structured related transfers, are reported by banks on a suspicion/limit basis, and all client records must be maintained for five years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Primary Operational USD Account (clearing hub for Stripe and Escrow_Pay settlements; digital banking and correspondent rails)
Capital Escrow Account (initial endowment custody) + Operational Private-Banking Account (foundation-friendly, strong international clientele)
Operational Account (second-line USD clearing; US and EU correspondent network; trade-finance desk)
Operational Account (Central American acquiring/e-commerce integration; BAC Credomatic card rails)
Operational Account (treasury and wire-processing desk; conservative but workable for e-commerce PIFs with full EDD files)
Capital Escrow Account / Wealth-Custody facility (limited current-account capacity; oriented to holding structures rather than active trading)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs and fintech wallet providers: LOW viability. Correspondent-bank de-risking, the absence of a Panama license, and the PIF's enhanced-due-diligence profile cause most offshore EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury-class providers) to reject or severely restrict Private Interest Foundations engaged in cross-border luxury resale. Panama-regulated fintechs licensed under Law 300 of 2022 (SBP 'Innovation Hub' and e-money/payment-license regime) offer MEDIUM-HIGH operational viability for USD digital wallets and payment aggregation, but they do not substitute for tier-1 bank clearing and are still required to apply full KYC/BO transparency. Legal constraint: any institution carrying out payment or e-money activity in Panama must hold an SBP license under Decree Law 9 of 1998; an unlicensed offshore EMI soliciting Panamanian customers, or a PIF using an unlicensed EMI to transact with Panamanian residents, creates regulatory and reputational exposure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Medium-strict mandate. Tier-1 banks (Banco General, Banistmo, BAC, Global Bank) generally require at least one authorized signatory and the ultimate beneficial owner to appear in person at a Panamanian branch for original signature execution on the account mandate; remote-only onboarding for a PIF is rarely approved on first engagement. Boutique private banks (Towerbank, St. Georges) may permit fully remote onboarding for beneficiaries from low-risk jurisdictions when the full corporate package (foundation charter, rights registry, BO declarations, and appointments) is apostilled and couriered wet-ink, followed by a secure videoconference due-diligence interview and enhanced source-of-funds review. Under SBP digital-onboarding rules (Rule 6-2022), identification can be performed electronically, but for an active e-commerce PIF in a Medium_Enhanced AML tier, physical attendance of the founder or a designated council member remains the lowest-friction path and materially shortens approval timelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation with non-registered beneficial ownership — risk of bearer-type foundation rights and opaque beneficiary decks (FATF Recommendation 24 breach in correspondents' assessment).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled foundation charter (Pacto Fundacional) filed with the Registro Público; certified Rights Registry (Registro de Derechos) proving issuance only of registered, non-bearer foundation rights with a complete holder ledger; sworn Beneficial Owner Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) under UAF Resolution 005-2015; legal opinion confirming abolition and immobilization of bearer instruments under Law 13 of 2017; CVs and passports of all foundation council members and the foundation guardian (if any).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 4791 vintage luxury resale — high transaction values, high frequency, counterfeit/stolen-goods and counterfeit-authentication risk; sector is a recognized money-laundering route in trade-based typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provenance dossier per inventory lot: original purchase receipts, third-party authentication certificates (Entrupy, Real Authentication, or equivalent), condition reports and chain-of-custody logs; independent valuation certificates for SKUs above USD 5,000; trademark or IP-owner consent where branding is used; platform-side records (Stripe, Escrow_Pay) evidencing genuine merchant-buyer interaction and no structured rapid flip of high-value items; quality-assurance SOP and returns/cancellation policy in Spanish and English.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce settlement rails (Stripe + Escrow_Pay) treated as 'third-party payments' — red flag for commingled customer funds, informal money transmission, and unlicensed escrow activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe Merchant Agreement and Escrow_Pay Master Services Agreement in the PIF's exact legal name; schema of money flow showing buyer -> platform -> PIF bank account with no interposition of anonymous third parties; monthly reconciliation statements mapping payouts to verified customer invoices; written policy prohibiting wire-chain 'through-account' transfers; UAF-compliant transaction monitoring and suspicious-activity reporting procedures; identification of the platforms' acquiring banks to satisfy the bank's correspondent due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection opacity — founder funds endowment/escrow account from mixed or overseas sources with ambiguous purpose (UAF 10k reporting threshold and SWIFT referral risk).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth statement with six months' bank statements for every contributor; SWIFT MT103 traces from the originating account; notarized and registered Deed of Endowment (Aporte Fundacional) stating the initial capital (bank-accepted minimum USD 1,000–10,000); evidence that endowed assets are traceable to lawful activity; pre-emptive narrative for any credit above USD 10,000 and pre-credit submission of a funds-flow diagram when aggregate funding exceeds USD 100,000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency and conduit mischaracterization — bank or correspondent mistakes the PIF for a Panama tax-resident commercial enterprise, causing CRS/FATCA misreporting, reputational flags, and potential withholding confusion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panamanian counsel tax opinion confirming territoriality, absence of Panama-source income from foreign online sales, and no effective management in Panama; current Aviso de Operación and nil/low income-tax returns to evidence good standing; CRS and FATCA self-certifications (CRS form and W-8BEN-E) with correct classification of the foundation; where the PIF qualifies as a reporting financial institution, a registered GIIN; board resolutions and records demonstrating that foundation administration and day-to-day management occur outside Panama.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) Founder or authorized contributor initiates a SWIFT MT103 from a bank in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction; field 50K must name the remitter (founder or disclosed contributor), field 59 must show the PIF's full legal name and Panama account number, and field 70/72 reference 'APORTE FUNDACIONAL — CONSTITUTION ENDOWMENT — [Registro Público foundation number]' to ensure clear classification as capital rather than commercial revenue. (2) Panama imposes no central-bank approval code, no FX declaration, and no convertibility certificate; the only mandatory layer is bank-level EDD, under which the PIF must supply the Apostilled foundation deed, the endowment resolution, and source-of-funds files before the first credit. (3) Credits of USD 10,000 or more are reported by the bank to the UAF; credits above USD 100,000 require a pre-credit funds-flow narrative from the foundation's counsel. (4) The remitting bank's own jurisdiction may apply its own outgoing-payment rules (e.g., EU/UK greater-transparency regimes), so the PIF should attach the foundation charter and a cover letter signed by counsel to prevent the transfer being rejected by the originator's compliance desk. (5) Capital escrow and operational accounts must never be intermingled: endowment funds sit in the Capital Escrow Account until the foundation council resolves to reallocate them to working capital, evidenced by a certified council minute.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Inventory and supplier settlements: use SWIFT MT103 (cover or serial method) with purpose narrative 'GOODS TRADE — SETTLEMENT OF VINTAGE LUXURY GOODS PURCHASE' and the beneficiary's full trade account; USD clearing executes via Panamanian banks' New York correspondents on Fedwire/CHIPS for same-day value. High-value single acquisitions (USD 25,000 and above, particularly with EU/UK boutique consignors) should use an irrevocable at-sight documentary letter of credit issued under UCP 600 by the Panama bank's trade-finance desk, payable against commercial invoice, authentication report, and transport/custody documents. Domestic Panamanian disbursements clear through the Cámara de Compensación Automatizada (ACH machinery operated via Banco Nacional de Panamá) in USD, while US-market disbursements can be routed via the bank's US dollar clearing account. Stripe and Escrow_Pay payouts arrive as platform settlements into the designated operational account; the PIF should maintain a rolling reserve buffer of approximately 6–10% of monthly volume to absorb chargebacks and the platforms' 180-day hold risk. All outbound wires above USD 10,000, or aggregate daily outflow above USD 20,000, require standing instruction files and, where the payee was not previously bank-verified, a source-of-funds and underlying-transaction dossier attached to the payment order.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) with licensed Panama banks or international counterparties under ISDA 2002 or a local master agreement — tenors to 24 months, no central clearing mandate.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) to match inventory-funding obligations where the PIF borrows or funds in USD but must discharge EUR/GBP supplier liabilities.
Plain-vanilla FX options (USD/EUR, USD/GBP) — permissible for contingent liabilities such as auction wins and competitive consignment purchases.

Non-deliverable forwards: not applicable for the Panamanian Balboa (fully convertible, USD-circulating, no offshore PAB NDF market); offshore USD/EUR or USD/GBP NDFs are legally permissible where a deliverable alternative is unavailable, but are economically inferior in Panama's zero-restriction environment.
Natural hedge through multi-currency operational accounts (EUR/GBP) at the Panama bank or a licensed EU/UK bank, limiting forced conversions and reducing reliance on derivative instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Panama Operation Tax (Franchise Tax) for Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before March 15; new foundations must pay within 90 days from the date of registry inscription
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a 5% monthly surcharge up to a maximum of 10%, plus interest; continued non-payment for three consecutive fiscal years results in administrative strike-off and possible dissolution by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate or Registered Agent licensed by the Panama Public Registry (Superintendencia de Registro Público)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the foundation anniversary date; immediate renewal required on any agent resignation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a resident registered agent for more than three consecutive months is cause for registry strike-off and administrative intervention; no separate government fee applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership / UBO Record Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (acting as AML/CFT record-keeper; records accessible to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero — UAF on lawful request)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in line with the foundation council anniversary; must be updated immediately upon any change in economic-leadership or beneficiary designation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, incomplete, or missing UBO records can result in administrative fines under Panama's legal transparency framework and, in serious cases, criminal liability for deliberate concealment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foundation Statutory Books and Registers Annual Internal Audit and Custody Certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Foundation Council and, when appointed, the Foundation Protector (internal governance review; no public filing unless judicially or regulatorily requested)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual review by foundation anniversary; continuous maintenance is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficient statutory records may dissolve the foundation's limitation-of-liability shield and expose the council members to personal liability; no fixed public filing penalty exists under Law 25 of 1995.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private Interest Foundations are not generally subject to compulsory audit under Law 25 of 1995; however, an independent certified audit becomes mandatory if the foundation carries on commercial operations with gross annual income above USD 2,000,000, or if total assets exceed USD 5,000,000, or if required by a financing counterparty, commercial license, foundation charter, or court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted in Panama; foundations maintaining records under the territorial income tax regime are expected to use full accrual accounting consistent with IFRS principles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Private Interest Foundations have no public annual UBO filing requirement. The registered agent must obtain, verify, and hold current beneficial ownership information, including any changes in council composition or designated beneficiaries, and must prepare an annual written UBO confirmation for internal records. Because PIFs do not issue share capital, annual shareholder-transfer confirmation is not applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation charter (Registro de Estatutos Fundamentales) and duly registered amendments
Foundation Council Minute Book / Resolution Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 1,200 depending on agent and level of service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for a dormant or low-activity PIF; if a voluntary or lender-required audit is performed, USD 2,500 - USD 6,500 depending on transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial tax regime: only Panama-source income is taxable. Foreign-source revenue of an online resale platform (sales of vintage luxury goods to non-Panamanian buyers, cross-border escrow settlements) is generally outside the corporate income tax net. Small taxpayers with annual gross income up to PAB 30,000 may elect a flat-rate regime of 12.5% on gross receipts in lieu of the net-income basis. No general tax holiday applies to ISIC 4791 e-commerce activity; the Private Interest Foundation itself is not a permitted commercial operator and enjoys no direct ISR exemption when it conducts prohibited trade, in which case the underlying operating Sociedad Anonima is the taxable entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 851 (Declaracion Jurada Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Juridicas) filed electronically via the DGI SITIO web portal (https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa) or the prior E-Tax 2.0 platform for taxpayers registered in the Registro Unico de Contribuyentes (RUC).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year accounting period, no later than 31 March of the following year. DGI may extend the general deadline through an official filing calendar based on the final RUC digit. The legal representative or resident agent of the Private Interest Foundation must file in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Valid RUC number, corporate name, fiscal year, and foundation registration certificate number in the Public Registry.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign founders must be identified in the UBO annex; enter the local licensed resident agent's data in the contact field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Twelve-month accounting period; must agree with the fiscal year registered in the DGI database.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deviation is allowed without prior DGI authorization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenue derived from economic activity performed in Panama: local consignment commissions, domestic resale proceeds, and platform fees attributable to Panamanian sellers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source internet sales and escrow settlements attributable to buyers located abroad; territorial sourcing applies only to activity carried out in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inventory acquisition costs of vintage luxury goods and direct fulfillment expenses matched to the Panama-source revenue reported in Box 3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cost of goods relating to foreign-source sales must be computed on a separate schedule and excluded from this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rent of the Panamanian establishment, payroll, Stripe and escrow payment-processing fees, logistics, marketing, depreciation, and financing costs deductible under Fiscal Code Articles 714-716.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deductions incurred in the production of Panama-source income are allocable; head-office charges from a foreign founder must satisfy transfer-pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 3 minus Boxes 4 and 5, adjusted for disallowed expenses and non-deductible provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foundation holds shares of a foreign resale company, foreign dividends are non-assessable and must not be included here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of prior-year tax losses, limited to a 5-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The carryforward reserve must be supported by audited schedules of prior Panama-source losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on net taxable income at the statutory 25% rate; for eligible small taxpayers, the alternative flat tax of 12.5% on gross income may be computed in the annex.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No credit is granted for foreign taxes unless a DTA containing an FTC provision applies to Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Monthly or quarterly advance ISR instalments, tax credits, and withholdings previously paid during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panamanian advance payments supported by DGI payment receipts may be credited.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due or refundable balance after credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a PIF that is reclassified as a taxable commercial entity, the final balance must be paid by the resident agent to avoid RUC suspension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the dividend withholding tax applicable to distributions from taxable or preferentially taxed profits (5% or 10%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends distributed to a non-resident founder are subject to Panamanian WHT at the moment of payment; DTA relief requires a valid TRC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of controlled transactions (Form 843) for cross-border purchase, commission, royalty, management, and financing arrangements with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when aggregate related-party transactions exceed PAB 1,000,000 in the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial ownership information required under Law 70 of 2019; identifies founders, foundation council members, and ultimate beneficiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign founders must provide the same UBO dataset to the local resident agent for electronic transmission to the UAF; failure to do so blocks filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus monthly interest at 1% per month or fraction. Non-filing leads to an official assessment, RUC deregistration, suspension of the Aviso de Operacion of the operating company, blocking of Stripe/Escrow merchant settlements, and criminal tax-evasion exposure of the foundation council.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 842-A (Declaracion de Pago Directo / advance ISR instalment) payable online through DGI SITIO or at authorized Panamanian banks.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly advance payment in June, September, December, and March; monthly for taxpayers with average net income above PAB 500,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are due by 30 June, 30 September, 31 December, and 31 March. The March instalment coincides with the final Form 851 deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated current-year Panama-source taxable income used as the base for the advance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source revenue of the PIF and of the cross-border resale operations must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% of estimated net taxable income, or 12.5% of gross income for taxpayers that validly elected the small-business flat-rate regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Election of the flat-rate regime is irreversible for the tax period and must be made before the first instalment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Deficiency penalties of 10% of the unpaid instalment, daily interest surcharges of 1% per month, and immediate collection via DGI coactive execution against banking assets.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% statutory dividend withholding tax where the profits have been subject to normal corporate income tax at 25%; 10% where the profits arise from income taxed under the alternative flat-rate regime or from exempt/offshore sources. Panama-signatory DTAs commonly cap the rate between 5% and 15%, with lower caps applicable to corporate shareholders of at least 10%-25% of the voting capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its fiscal authority; (2) deliver the TRC and a completed DGI relief application to the Panamanian payer or resident agent before the dividend or interest payment date; (3) allow the payer to attach the documentation to the corresponding DGI return; (4) for refunds of excess WHT, file a claim with the DGI International Taxation Unit within the statutory limitation window, typically three years from the withholding event; and (5) renew the TRC annually for ongoing distributions. Panama's in-force treaties include agreements with the United Kingdom, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Switzerland, Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, United Arab Emirates, Italy, France, Ireland, Qatar, Portugal, Israel, and Barbados; the specific rate must be verified on the treaty's Protocol and the Domestic Savings Clause.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty WHT for the use of trademarks, copyrights, or know-how in Panama: effective 12.5% of the gross royalty, calculated as a deemed 50% taxable base subject to the 25% ISR; DTAs commonly reduce the rate to 10%. Interest paid by Panamanian entities to non-resident lenders on loans used in Panama: statutory WHT of 5% under the Law 76 of 2019 regime; bank deposit interest paid to foreign depositors is exempt. Interest and royalties sourced abroad (loan agreement executed and funds disbursed outside Panama for a foreign borrower) fall outside the Panamanian territorial WHT net. All treaty reductions require a valid TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation and the Form 843 related-party schedule are mandatory when annual controlled transactions exceed PAB 1,000,000, or when the taxpayer's gross income exceeds PAB 9,000,000. The Master File is required for members of a multinational group whose consolidated group revenue exceeds PAB 250,000,000. These thresholds derive from Executive Decree 401 of 2011, as amended by Law 76 of 2019 and supplementary DGI regulations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations for all entities, but the territorial tax regime de facto requires substantive local activity to generate taxable Panama-source revenue. Since Law 70 of 2019, every juridical person, including a Private Interest Foundation, must keep a compliant beneficial ownership file; the foundation must also appoint and maintain a licensed resident agent, a registered office in Panama, a full accounting ledger, and a foundation council with authority exercised from Panama. Critically, Article 25 of Law 25 of 1995 prohibits the PIF from engaging in commercial activity; operating an ISIC 4791 online resale business in the foundation itself is unlawful. The permitted structure is a Panamanian Sociedad Anonima holding the Aviso de Operacion, employees, inventory, and payment-processor contracts, with the PIF acting solely as shareholder or beneficiary holder of that operating company; if the PIF directly executes the e-commerce trade, the DGI may reclassify the foundation as a taxable commercial entity, cancel its registration, and impose penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Panama-source online consignment and resale revenue from Form 851; fabrication of vintage-luxury purchase invoices; routing Stripe or Escrow Pay settlements through a foreign account of the PIF to hide taxable commissions; inflating COGS with non-arm's-length intercompany invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to PAB 50,000 in addition to the 10% late filing surcharge and 1% monthly interest; administrative assessment by the DGI followed by coactive seizure of bank accounts and luxury inventory; criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years under the Fiscal Code anti-evasion provisions; publication of the tax lien in official registries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and the ultimate founder are subject to civil joint and several liability for the evaded tax; a Panamanian court may pierce the PIF's legal personality under Law 25 of 1995 Articles 8 and 9; directors face imprisonment, judicial travel bans (prohibicion de salida del pais), and asset freezing orders triggered by criminal tax proceedings.
